messages:
alex: Ran a 4xA100 nsys run against the redispatcher + kv-prefetch branch. Seeing repeated micro-gaps in the multi-GPU timeline during prompt streaming. Trace: https://perfetto.redwood/trace/AB12. Quick grab of the timeline below.

sam: can you paste the nsys flags you used? wondering if NCCL sampling was enabled.

alex: Sure — command I used: 
```
nsys profile --output=run_redispatch.qdrep --trace=cuda,nvtx,nccl --sample=none 
  --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --capture-range-end=stop 
  --force-overwrite --stats=true 
  ./bin/serve_load_test --model llama-13b --gpus=4 --qps=80 --seq=1024 --batcher=experimental_redispatcher
```
Note: I disabled sample-based collection to keep timelines deterministic.

jia: looked at the qdrep — interesting pattern. During iterations where kv cache handshake triggers, the per-GPU kernel stream shows a short memcopy + small kernel (kv_handshake_copy, kv_apply_delta) that is interleaved right before reduce_scatter. That lines up with ~1.2ms of effective gap in the all-reduce windows.

alex: exactly. The weird bit is that the kernel selector seems to pick a different matmul kernel variant (matmul_fp16_v2_small) right after the handshake, then we redispatch back to matmul_fp16_v1 for larger batches. The selector transition creates a small stall on stream 7 while we load the new kernel and update kernel arguments.

maria: :thinking: Are we sure it's the selector load and not the batching heuristic splitting the batch across two dispatch calls? If batcher splits mid-microbatch we would see two consecutive collective ops with a small gap by design.

alex: Good point. I instrumented NVTX around the batching boundary and saw NVTX markers: 
```
NVTX: [BATCHER_START id=842]
NVTX: [REDISPATCH_DECIDE kernel=matmul_fp16_v2_small]
NVTX: [KV_HANDSHAKE start]
NVTX: [REDISPATCH_APPLY]
NVTX: [COLLECTIVE reduce_scatter start]
```
The ordering suggests the redispatch decision happens before the handshake, so selector + handshake interplay looks suspicious.

sam: Any NCCL timeline evidence? ring vs tree?

jia: NCCL shows reduce_scatter_ring and allreduce_ring windows are split across GPUs with ~1.1-1.6ms gaps. I aligned the GPU timestamps and saw the gaps correlate with a device-side memcpy from host to device for KV refresh. The memcpy preempts the kernel stream slightly because we use the same stream for small copies right now. If we move handshake copies to a dedicated high-priority stream or async pinned-buffer path, it might vanish.

perf-bot: Auto-detect: multiple short memcpy events observed on default stream during collective windows. Suggest low-overhead prefetch using cudaMemcpyAsync + dedicated streams.

maria: Repro steps we should try:
- reproduce with REDWOOD_BATCHER=stable (no redispatcher) to confirm baseline
- run with handshake copies on high-priority stream (quick patch in local branch)
- toggle kernel cache warming (preload selector kernels at startup)

alex: I already ran the baseline: with stable batcher the gaps disappear. With preloading kernels (simple cudaLaunchKernel warmup loop at startup), gaps reduce by ~40% but don't go away. With handshake copies moved to a dedicated stream, the gap disappears in this load test.

sam: That suggests two root causes: (1) batching + redispatch cause extra crossing points, and (2) copying on the default stream blocks the collective windows. Both need fixes.

jia: Proposed short-term fixes:
- change kv-prefetch to use dedicated high-priority stream for host->device copies (low risk)
- add kernel-warmup pass in redispatcher init to avoid selector cold path (medium risk)
- change batching heuristic to prefer keeping microbatches with the same kernel variant coalesced (higher risk, needs QA)

alex: I'll open a PR with the first two patches and attach updated nsys traces. PR branch: feature/redispatch-fix/kv-stream-warmup

maria: Please include a perfetto share link and a short reproducer script. Also add a small unit test that asserts no memcpy events on default stream during critical collective windows (we can check NVTX markers + cudaEvent offsets).

alex: Will do. Uploading traces and a short reproducer in the PR. Thanks for the triage folks :thumbsup:

sam: Nice work. After PR lands we should run a full soak with dedupe/shard-workload to ensure no regression under varied seq lengths.

jia: Agreed. I can run the soak on the 4-GPU dev farm once PR is ready.

perf-bot: Reminder: schedule a nightly nsys sweep for the redispatch branch to catch regressions automatically (will create ticket).

alex: filing follow-up ticket with timeline screenshots and commands.
